function: function: a learned transformer classifier, trained by continual learning, recognizes human activities from Wi-Fi uplink CSI (discriminative sensing); it designs no beams, waveforms, or resources and estimates no channel (p. 2, p. 4, p. 10).
notes: Exclude, code function. The learned method (EdgeCL: transformer discriminator trained sequentially with distilled core-set replay and sharpness-aware optimization) maps CSI sequences to activity classes. p. 2: "the ED uses the uplink CSI to sense each user. Here, we focus on general discriminative sensing tasks"; p. 4: "probability vectors for C classes of user activities"; p. 10: "we collect an HAR dataset by using a practical wireless ISAC system". CSI-based human activity recognition is a sensing function outside the seven areas: it does not set beams, waveforms, or resources (area 5), and the CSI is measured with PicoScenes rather than estimated by the method (area 2, p. 10). Earlier codes do not apply: a research article (not a survey), the method is learned, and the learning is no network decision such as offloading or scheduling (above_phy). For the reviewer: the system does communicate (802.11ac Wi-Fi uplink traffic of a Zoom meeting, p. 10), so the example 'sensing alone in a system that does not communicate' does not apply literally; the exclusion rests on the learned function matching no area. The PDF is arXiv 2502.12736v2; Crossref gives the same title and the same four authors for the DOI (IEEE Trans. Wireless Commun.).
